title: Analysis of Lysophagic Flux in Cultured Induced Neurons using RFP-GFP-galectin3
author: Vinay Eapen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bx48pqzw

steps.title: Prepare transfection mix
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL buffer R to a sterile 1.5 mL tube, add 0.5 µg pAC150 GFP‑RFP‑LGALS3 (or R186S) vector and 0.5 µg pCMV‑hyPBase hyperactive piggyBac vector, pipet up/down to mix, and let sit at room temperature for 10 min. This mixture is sufficient for two transfections (one 6‑well).

steps.title: Dissociate cells with Accutase
steps.instruction: Treat cultured cells with Accutase, then neutralize the enzyme with five volumes of E8 medium containing ROCK inhibitor.

steps.title: Count and collect cells
steps.instruction: Count cells and collect 2 × 10⁵ cells for each transfection.

steps.title: Pellet cells
steps.instruction: Spin down the counted cells, allow residual medium to settle at the tube bottom; if excess residue remains, remove it with a P200 pipette.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in buffer R
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet to a concentration of 2 × 10⁵ cells per 5 mL (equivalent to 4 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹) using buffer R, accounting for any remaining residue volume.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel‑coated 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Coat a 6‑well plate with Matrigel, add 2 mL E8 medium containing ROCK inhibitor (1:1000) to each well that will be used; two transfections will be combined into one well.

steps.title: Set up Neon electroporation system
steps.instruction: Wipe the Neon pipette station with ethanol and place it inside the biosafety hood; add 3 mL electrolytic buffer (buffer E) to the Neon tube, insert the tube into the station until a click is felt.

steps.title: Select electroporation program
steps.instruction: Choose program 13 on the Neon device (Voltage 1100 V, Pulse width 20 ms, Pulse number 2); program 9 may also be used.

steps.title: Combine cells with plasmid mix
steps.instruction: Mix 10–11 mL of the resuspended cells with the plasmid‑containing R‑buffer so that the final volume is 21–22 mL.

steps.title: Electroporate first cell aliquot
steps.instruction: Load a Neon tip, slowly pipet 10 mL of the cell‑plasmid mixture into the tip, and electroporate using program 13 while avoiding air bubbles; insert the tip gently until the click is felt, then depress the plunger slowly.

steps.title: Handle air bubbles (if any)
steps.instruction: If an air bubble appears in the tip, remove the tip, expel all liquid, and repipet the mixture before electroporation.

steps.title: Transfer electroporated cells to plate
steps.instruction: Immediately after electroporation, dispense the entire content into one well of the prepared 6‑well plate without pipetting up and down with the Neon tip.

steps.title: Electroporate second aliquot
steps.instruction: Using the same tip, repeat the loading and electroporation with the remaining cell mixture and add this second electroporated suspension to the same well.

steps.title: Seed and incubate cells
steps.instruction: Disperse cells evenly within the well and place the plate in a low‑oxygen incubator for 2 days.

steps.title: Differentiate to induced neurons
steps.instruction: Follow the published protocol “Neural differentiation of AAVS1‑TREG3‑NGN2 pluripotent stem cells” (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br9em93e) to convert the electroporated cells into induced neurons (iN).

steps.title: Plate iNs for imaging
steps.instruction: When cultures reach ~90 % confluence between days 5–7, plate cells onto 35 mm glass‑bottom dishes (MatTek, No. 1.5, 14 mm diameter) at approximately 1 × 10⁵ cells per 2 mL dish.

steps.title: Prepare for LLoMe treatment (Day 12)
steps.instruction: Two hours before LLoMe addition, remove 0.75 mL of media from each well, save it as “condition media”, and add 0.75 mL fresh ND2 medium so that each well contains 5 mL total.

steps.title: Add LLoMe
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL fresh ND2/LLoMe solution to achieve a final LLoMe concentration of 500 mM in 2 mL; incubate cells for 1 h.

steps.title: Replace LLoMe media
steps.instruction: Remove the LLoMe‑containing media and replace it with a mixture of the saved condition media and fresh ND2 medium (for each 0.75 mL of condition media add 1.25 mL fresh ND2), resulting in 2 mL of LLoMe‑free medium per well.

steps.title: Post‑treatment wash and fixation
steps.instruction: After 12 h, wash cells once with 1× PBS, then fix with 4 % paraformaldehyde in PBS for 15 min at room temperature; replace the fixation solution with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Image cells by confocal microscopy
steps.instruction: Image cells at room temperature on a Yokogawa CSU‑X1 spinning‑disk confocal mounted on a Nikon Ti‑E inverted microscope (Nikon Perfect Focus System, Plan Apo 40×/1.30 NA or 100×/1.40 NA objectives), using 488 nm (100 mW) and 561 nm (100 mW) lasers controlled by AOTF, capture images with a Hamamatsu ORCA‑ER camera and MetaMorph software.

steps.title: Generate maximum‑projection images
steps.instruction: Display Z‑series as maximum‑intensity projections and save the images using Fiji (ImageJ).

steps.title: Quantify LGALS3 puncta with CellProfiler
steps.instruction: Run the provided CellProfiler pipeline: identify primary objects 200–1000 pixel units for each cell, identify primary objects 2–20 pixel units for LGALS3 puncta using a robust background threshold, measure object size/shape, and assign each punctum to its parent cell to obtain puncta‑per‑cell values.

steps.title: Adjust image brightness and export
steps.instruction: Apply identical brightness/contrast adjustments to each channel, convert the stacks to RGB, and save the final images with Fiji for publication.

steps.title: Select hygromycin‑resistant cells
steps.instruction: Four days post‑electroporation, add hygromycin B at 50 mg mL⁻¹, maintain cells in selection medium for 7–10 days until no cell death is observed and all cells have integrated the GFP‑RFP‑LGALS3 construct.
